checks.conclusion: The block owns exactly two stable viewport records and reserves scene, lifetime, first viewport and replacement viewport admissions during preparation. Constructor input checks and validate_prepared run before the outer token is moved and execution begins. Scene credit enters in-place owner preparation; viewport[0] enters raw B71A80; lifetime credit enters success-only reference construction; viewport[1] enters the replacement factory. Every consume uses this attempt's field, with no ambient next-slot mechanism or new host allocation on the supported path.

Prepared moves transfer the capability; moving an executing attempt is rejected. Prepared cancellation releases credits and forgets only unexposed cancelled/unused records, returning the block to idle. Constructor-local destruction after execution cancels only remaining credits and marks the block settled. It preserves all camera companions and published viewport records; it performs no native release, pool return or object deletion.

checks.topic: Prepared owner abandonment and camera survivors
checks.conclusion: Before camera completion, constructor cleanup resets only an owner still in prepared phase, ending unused typed/scene preparation before returning the raw pool slot. A callee-unwound dead owner remains in the block for explicit reset. Late B71A80 failure can leave viewport[0] live after camera typed storage ends; settlement preserves that record and reset rejects it using Storage::phase without reading ended camera storage. After successful B71A80, camera_completed prevents a diagnostic during reference admission from freeing the live camera or returning its slot; the resulting unsupported diagnostic can pin the block for external recovery.

The string live bit is cleared before normal or unwinding string return. Camera publication switches to base state before normal string cleanup. The replacement factory owns failure of its raw viewport construction; after successful factory return the caller switches to base state and has no automatic local viewport release on a subsequent exception. Constructor catch performs only its projected string/raw-camera/helper-base cleanup, then rethrows; nested throwing cleanup terminates. Token settlement remains outside that native cleanup and does not add survivor releases.

checks.conclusion: Each configuration/replacement operation reloads the helper's current camera key and resolves its live canonical NativeCameraReference, permitting a callback to substitute another supported camera without falling back to the original block owner. It reads the current borrowed decrement IAT cell at the release site, then checks the current concrete profile/table only on zero. The explicit release context supplies those current inputs without introducing a shared registry API or extra native retain.

The reference disposal callback is fixed to the stable block before publication and only marks retirement after native camera deletion and identity-only runtime unbind. It validates host reference/owner identity and dead phase without reading the returned native pool slot. Reset requires settled phase, retired reference/dead owner where present, and both records unused/cancelled/retired. It destroys the retired reference before the dead owner and forgets inert viewport records only under caller-established host quiescence. Live orphans, prepared/executing reuse and destruction of a non-idle block are rejected; helper deletion does not authorize reclaiming the block.
